zh.title: 飛航雷射光干擾通報連續三年下降仍偏高
zh.summary: 美國飛航雷射光干擾連續三年下降；二○二六年已通報四四七○起
body: 美國聯邦航空總署（FAA）表示，國家空域系統中通報的雷射光干擾事件連續第三年下降，機師於二○二六年通報了四四七○起，較去年同期減少二四％。
FAA指出，該機構與地方、州及聯邦執法單位合作進行宣導與訓練，以打擊雷射光干擾事件；此類干擾於二○二三年曾達歷史新高的一三三○四起。
FAA亦提醒公眾，節日期間朝天空發射的雷射光展示可能構成安全風險，集中的雷射光束可能使飛行員分心或暫時失明。
FAA表示，自二○一○年開始追蹤雷射光干擾報告以來，飛行員已通報三二二起受傷事件；朝飛機發射雷射光屬聯邦犯罪，每次違規最高可處一萬一千美元罰款。

en.title: Pilot-Reported Laser Strikes Fall for Third Straight Year, Still Too High, FAA Says
en.summary: Pilot-reported laser strikes fell for a third year; 4,470 reported in 2026 through July
body: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) reported that pilot-reported laser strikes in the National Airspace System have declined for the third consecutive year, with 4,470 strikes reported in 2026, a 24 percent decrease from the same point last year.
The FAA said it conducts outreach and training with local, state, and federal law enforcement, and that strikes reached an all-time high of 13,304 in 2023.
The agency warned that holiday laser-light displays can pose a safety risk when aimed into the sky, as concentrated beams can distract or temporarily blind pilots.
The FAA stated that 322 injuries have been reported since it began tracking laser strike data in 2010. Shining a laser at an aircraft is a federal crime, with fines up to $11,000 per violation.
